items.author: Ben
items.title: Rivals buy firms too - buy_corporation joins the scored-utility candidate list
items.design: The symmetry half of BL-628 (whole-firm buyout), and a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in its established shape: deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, a legal verb and never a planner. THE WORK: score buy_corporation in corp_ai.cpp's existing candidate list, capped at one acquisition per evaluation, its price carried in the candidate's spend under the solvency gate so a rival cannot buy itself below its reserve floor. Availability is gated on the target's ownership class, not on the acquirer's cash - the 'never on cash' ruling's shape. Record the grant in the standing rules with its date, as every prior widening is recorded. SAVING UP IS NOT PLANNING, and this item owns the distinction: Ben's Sprint 20 goal wants a corp to accumulate cash toward an acquisition, but a scorer that defers a cheap build today in order to afford a firm tomorrow is edging toward the planner the standing rules forbid. The honest route needs no new machinery - accumulation is EMERGENT when the buy candidate outscores the marginal build, since a tick with no affordable positive candidate simply banks its cash. Whether that actually happens at the authored weights is a measurement, and BL-634 (acquisition viability) is where it is taken.

items.title: The Corporations panel does not fit its column - names cut to one letter, Declare Hostile clipped
items.author: Ben
items.design:
OBSERVED LIVE, 2026-08-26 (BL-633's capture), and pre-existing - BL-633 changed no width and no column count. Five columns carrying 62+62+62+220 px of fixed width do not fit the shell fold-out column (380-460 px by resolution) at 1280x720: the Corporation NAME column collapses to a single letter ('F', 'E', 'C') and the Stance column's 'Declare Hostile' button clips off the right edge as 'De...'. This is BL-449's shape exactly - the surface that shipped clean on a compile AND a 36/36 harness while being unusable - still live in the same panel. THE WORK: re-budget the columns against shell_column_width(disp.x) rather than fixed pixels, and decide whether the stance presses belong in-row at this width at all or behind the row's Selection drill. Note NR-663: expect_no_clipping did NOT catch this, because ImGui SmallButton labels are not instrumented into the overflow ledger - so this needs a real look, not a green row.

SUPERSEDED IN PLACE BY BL-674 (diplomacy by stance), 2026-08-29 - newest-dated wins, and this is recorded rather than quietly applied. BL-674 carries Ben's instruction to DELETE the Reach, Share and Stance columns and group the rows by stance instead, which removes the starvation this item proposed to re-budget: three of the five columns stop existing, so there is no fixed-width budget left to blow. This item's second half - whether the stance presses belong in-row at this width - is answered there too (they move into the row's own action affordance and keep their confirms). Left open rather than closed because Ben owns the close; do not build BL-639 and BL-674 as two changes to one file.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

items.title: Finish the dissolution walk - ground follows the firm, and hoist the duplicated HQ rule
items.author: Ben
items.design: Two loose ends the wave-2 review barrier found in BL-628, neither a defect today. (1) world::province_holder takes a CORP id via battle_system.cpp's field_held_by, and dissolve_into's inventory does not carry it. Entity ids are monotonic with no recycling, so a stale holder is inert rather than aliasing - but R4's wording is 'no dangling reference survives', and ground is PROPERTY, so it TRANSFERS. Now written into FINANCE.md's three-way rule, which also gained a fourth outcome, KEEP, for the historical record - history is not property and is never rewritten, which is the one place a reference to the erased corp survives on purpose. Extend the harness fixture to hold a province, since it currently never constructs one. (2) recompute_hq in corp_command.cpp DUPLICATES designate_hq/corp_home_body from corporation_generation.cpp, including kProjectedReachUnits = 2.5f - unavoidable at authoring because another slice owned that file in the same wave. Both have landed; the review verified them line-for-line identical. Hoist to a shared seam so they cannot drift.

items.title: charter_reach is computed at generation and silently zeroed on load
items.author: Ben
items.design: Found by the wave-2 review barrier. BL-638 added settlement_state::charter (a charter_reach), and w_settlement/r_settlement do not carry it. The omission is SYMMETRIC so the stream stays consistent and no version bump is owed - it is not a corruption bug. It is a LATENT one: the field is silently zeroed on load, which is benign only while the sole readers are generate_corporations and its harness, both of which run before any save exists. It becomes wrong the moment BL-627 (profitability ledger), BL-629 (rival acquisition) or the generation ledger reads charter off a LOADED world - and it will read as 'this world has no charter' rather than as an error. TWO HONEST ROUTES, pick one and say why: serialise it (a version bump, claimed through next_save_version.js), or RECOMPUTE it on load from the ladder it is derived from, which costs no format change and cannot drift from its source. The second is probably right, since charter_reach is a pure function of already-serialised state.

items.title: A demand injector that cannot price a basket entry must SAY SO, not skip it
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE MECHANISM THAT MADE TWO SEPARATE BUGS INVISIBLE ON THE SAME DAY, which is why it is an item rather than a note. inject_population_demand and inject_background_demand both SKIP a basket entry whose resource carries no market base price - silently, with no warning and no row anywhere. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: (1) BL-649's census read as having no background demand at all on its first run, and (2) tools/verify/spawn_solvency.cpp - whose own header says it loads world_gen.lua and did not - measured BL-635's entire spawn diagnosis in a world where background demand did not exist. Neither failed. Both just quietly answered a question about a different world. THE WORK: an injector that cannot price a basket entry must report it - a named diagnostic on the first occurrence, and a harness row that FAILS on a basket naming an unpriced good, since that combination is always either a missing script or an authoring error and is never intended. A basket entry is a STATEMENT that somebody wants the good; silently dropping it turns a design statement into a no-op. Cheap, and it protects every measurement the rest of Sprint 21 depends on.

items.title: The eighth field - a return sees the whole quarter, not just the money loop
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling, 2026-08-26, on NR-655/NR-668 - option A of the three-way fork, and the measurement that forced it: a firm earning through mercenary contracts files a trailing_net IDENTICAL to a firm that earns nothing there, so BL-628's buyout undervalues it by exactly 640 credits (k 8.0 x the 80/quarter the record cannot see). Design in FINANCE.md section The eighth field. THE WORK: add `other` to quarterly_return = the whole-tick balance delta minus the money-loop net, and MOVE THE FILING from the end of apply_budget to after the tick's last balance mover - which is the part that needs care, since apply_budget does not own the tick and the headless harnesses call it directly. Then re-point corp_trailing_net at the mean of (net + other) so the buyout prices off the whole quarter. THREE PROPERTIES TO ASSERT: the seven flows still explain `net` unchanged; net+other telescopes EXACTLY over a run (the retain property extended from one function to the whole tick); and BL-628's own harness row that currently PINS the 640-credit blindness must be re-specified to pin the closure instead - do not delete it, invert it. `other` is deliberately NOT itemised: split into named lines it becomes a second budget breakdown competing with corp_budget, and the reason there is one accounting authority is that two of them disagree. Versions the save format.

items.title: A short pool buys on the market, up to a reservation ceiling
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE BLOCKER UNDER BL-641, AND PROBABLY UNDER FOUR MORE CHANNELS. Measured 2026-08-26: with building upkeep rates on, operating firms went 227 -> 19, because the goods drawn are produced 0.0 in band and a POOL DRAW never reaches market_component::demand - so the want never becomes a price, no rival scores the building that would supply it, and the sink starves itself. run_construction and run_processing already bid; run_unit_upkeep does not and carries the same latent defect. DESIGN-OWED, and the open question is Ben's because it widens FINANCE.md: should a goods draw place real demand on the market when the pool is short - and if so, does it BUY (spending credits, which makes upkeep a market participant) or merely SIGNAL (raising price without a transaction, which is cheaper but invents demand nobody pays for)? The first is coherent and expensive; the second is a thumb on the scale and should probably be refused on the same grounds the project refuses clamps. Until this is settled, BL-641's rates stay at 0.0 and every remaining channel (BL-643 infrastructure, BL-644 state, BL-645 research, BL-646 conflict) should be checked against property 3 before it is built, not after. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-08-26): 'Buy on the market, but at a threshold, buying is not allowed. This goes hand in hand with maximum and minimum prices for goods.' And ONE RULE FOR EVERY GOODS DRAW - unit upkeep takes the same shape, not a second one. Written into MARKETS.md section Settled: a short pool BUYS, up to a reservation ceiling. THE WORK: a short pool bids the shortfall into market_component::demand and pays for what it gets; above the ceiling it does not bid at all and the existing shortfall rule weakens the building (or unit) instead. The ceiling is authored in the PRICE BAND family beside floor_mult/ceil_mult, not in upkeep - it is a statement about what a good is worth paying, not about who is buying - and its value is MEASURED against the census and the operating-firm count, never guessed. It is the exact mirror of BL-386's seller-side floor_price: both sides may decline a trade, neither may dictate one. Turning BL-641's rates non-zero is gated on this landing.

items.title: Decide what actually shapes background density - the ratio, or the per-resource cap
items.author: Ben
items.design: Raised by BL-655's measurement and by its novelty flag. Pass 6 is documented as stopping on a 0.90 production/demand ratio, described as 'an emergent measurement rather than an injected clearing constant' and 'a stop condition, not a firm-count budget'. MEASURED: the ratio NEVER BINDS on the worlds we generate. `per_resource_firm_cap = 8` binds on every demanded resource, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x basket breadth - which reproduced 104, 64 and 56 corps exactly across three configurations. Its own comment still says 'provisional - measure, then pin'. The doc has been corrected to describe what the code does; what is OPEN is which behaviour is wanted. THREE READINGS: (a) the cap is the real design and the ratio is dead weight - pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and delete the ratio; (b) the ratio is the real design and the cap is an emergency brake set too low - raise it until the ratio binds, which restores the 'calibrated, not authored' property the doc claims; (c) both, with the cap as a genuine guard against a pathological basket. Note the consequence either way: under (a) density becomes a function of how many DIFFERENT goods are wanted, so every demand channel Sprint 21 adds moves the world's size - which may be a feature.

items.title: A firm underwater long enough exits - give interest the consequence it is supposed to have
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED 2026-08-26 from Ben's own observation of the live build. Of 12 seeds, 3 clear with ZERO interest; the 9 that fail all dipped negative once and interest is then 43-60% of their whole loss, against an operating gap of only -24 to -40 cr/qtr. 1.02^80 = 4.9x over the warm start. The rate is not the defect - components.hpp's 'no insolvency consequence' is. A firm that would have died in year three trades for twenty and is handed to the player as wreckage. THE WORK: a firm underwater for N consecutive quarters EXITS - dissolved, or absorbed via BL-628's dissolve_into, which already moves holdings, pools, balance and returns and cancels the promises nobody is left to keep. N and the trigger are authored in economy.lua and MEASURED, not picked. DESIGN-OWED on three questions that are Ben's: (1) dissolve or absorb - absorption by a solvent neighbour is richer and reuses the buyout path, dissolution is simpler and leaves ground free; (2) does this run IN PLAY as well as in the pre-game, i.e. can the player's own corp fail - NR-670 already ruled a rival may not BUY the player out, and this is a different question about the player failing on their own account; (3) what happens to the ground and the workforce - a dissolved firm's tiles should probably become available rather than stay held. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is priority A: the field at seat time becomes self-selected for viability, so BL-630's shortlist floor should start being met instead of falling through to its fallback on 23 of 24 seeds.

items.title: The solvency gate tests the price, not the position after the debt transfers
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED by BL-634, which found it by taking its own brief's gate literally. The acquisition price is max(0, book_value + k x trailing_net + balance) and the balance term is SIGNED, so a deeply indebted firm's negative cash cancels its book value, the sum goes below zero, and the floor hands it over FREE. On 5 of 8 seeds the cheapest buyable firm cost exactly 0 cr. The dissolution rule then transfers the debt at face value: one seed took on -13,358 cr for nothing, and 3 of 8 buyers that bought the cheapest firm were sunk by it. THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BUG - a worthless firm is worth nothing, and NR-648's reasoning stands. The bug is that the SOLVENCY GATE READS THE PRICE rather than the buyer's balance AFTER the transfer, which is the same shape as the non-finite-price bug BL-628 caught in its own code: a check applied to the wrong quantity. THE WORK: gate on the post-acquisition position, so a corp cannot be handed a liability it could never have chosen to take on. Then re-run acquisition_viability's --target cheapest sweep, where 'still earning after' should go 5/8 -> 8/8. Note the harness already measures BOTH gates and its --target flag exists for exactly this comparison.

items.title: Population lens: regional heatmap with harder scaling, not a per-tile mark
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "Population: Let's see what this looks like as a heatmap with more extreme scaling. This way we should be able to see population regionally, not just on each tile."

Today the lens draws "per-tile value marks, workforce efficiency" (LENSES.md routing table) - a per-tile read, which is why a region of moderate population and a region of none look similar at whole-planet zoom. Two changes: a continuous heatmap fill rather than discrete marks, and a scaling curve steep enough that regional differences separate instead of compressing into the middle of the ramp.

EXPLICITLY AN EXPERIMENT, in Ben's own framing - "let's see what this looks like". The deliverable is a capture to rule on, not a settled design; expect a second pass on the curve. Worth measuring the actual population distribution first so the curve is fitted to the data rather than guessed - the same discipline BL-649's census brought to demand.

items.title: Scarcity lens: drop the dead Opportunity code, reuse its glyph, render market scarcity per resource
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "I support changing opportunity to scarcity. Drop the old code, reuse the glyph, and render market scarcity per resource."

READ AS: the lens KEEPS the name Scarcity - the earlier idea of renaming it to Opportunity is dropped - while the retired Opportunity lens's leftovers are deleted and its GLYPH is reused for Scarcity. Recorded explicitly because the instruction can be read in both directions, and because the session had just flagged that Opportunity is a name BL-604 retired; if this reading is wrong it is a one-line revert.

WHY A GLYPH MATTERS HERE: Scarcity is keyboard-cycle only, which is why Ben listed it among the lenses needing glyphs. icons::opportunity survives in src/ui/icons.{hpp,cpp} with no caller since BL-604, so the mark exists and is unused - reusing it costs nothing and lets Scarcity earn a strip slot, since LENSES.md's rule is that an on-screen lens carries one distinct glyph.

Also dead and worth removing in the same sweep, though Ben named only Opportunity: icons::country (BL-601) and icons::production (BL-604), neither of which has a caller.

The behaviour half - "render market scarcity per resource" - may already hold: the lens draws "per-market shortfall blocks + key" keyed to the selected resource, and the 2026-08-28 sweep captured scarcity_lens_full_iron and _steel. Confirm before changing anything; the glyph may be the whole of the real work.

items.title: Give every strip-eligible lens a distinct glyph (Company; Supply, Supply-routes, Reach deferred)
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "It looks like we need to add glyphs for scarcity, supply, supply-routes, and reach."

SCOPE NARROWED BY BEN THE SAME DAY: "I don't think we need body-to-body lenses yet. Keep the code but ignore for this session." Supply, Supply-routes and Reach are all body-to-body, so their glyphs are deferred with them - the code stays, the work waits. Scarcity is covered by BL-662 (it inherits the Opportunity mark).

WHAT REMAINS LIVE HERE IS THE COMPANY LENS, added 2026-08-28. It borrows icons::corporation while keyboard-only, on the precedent Reach and Supply-routes set. It cannot join the on-screen strip until it has its own mark, because Corp would be its immediate neighbour and LENSES.md forbids two strip neighbours sharing a glyph. A company is a background firm, so the mark wants to read as smaller/plural against the corporation's single solid form.

Three glyphs are dead and free to cannibalise: icons::country, icons::opportunity (claimed by BL-662), icons::production.

items.title: The labour read has no home, and wage competition is invisible
items.author: Claude
items.design:
FILED SO A FINDING IS NOT DELETED ALONG WITH THE SURFACE THAT DISPLAYED IT WRONGLY. BL-676 retires the Economy panel on Ben's 2026-08-29 call. Two of its three views were duplicates and one was a visibility breach, but the Workforce view was answering a real question badly rather than answering a redundant one - and after the deletion nothing answers it at all.

WHAT THE CAPTURE PASS MEASURED. The workforce table drew eighteen rows and every single one read "82% (labour short)". The panel's own doc had warned the mock fixture was uniform at 85% and said explicitly: verify against the live sim, not the CSV. Verified against the live sim - it is uniform there too.

AND IT IS NOT A BUG. `report.workforce_contention` is the POOL-LEVEL min(1, supply/demand) keyed (corp, body), and every corp in the fixture holds on one body, so one pool yields one number correctly repeated eighteen times. The view is not broken; it is showing a quantity that cannot vary in the situation it is shown in.

THE ACTUAL FINDING: BL-614 (wage competition) SUPERSEDED that scalar and nothing surfaces what replaced it. economy_system.cpp says so in terms - when a pool is contended the uniform proportional scalar no longer applies; scarce labour allocates building by building, offered wage descending (base_wage x (1 + wage_bid)), building id ascending on a tie, each granted up to its demand until the pool is spent. The marginal building takes a partial grant and those below it get nothing. The factor a building actually runs at is `report.building_labour[id]`, and the pool aggregate survives only as a reporting figure.

So there is a real mechanic here - bidding for scarce labour, and losing a building's shift to a rival who bid higher - and the only surface that ever mentioned labour rendered it as one number eighteen times. `building_labour[id]` is per building and varies; it is the quantity a player would act on.

DESIGN-OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED HERE. Where this lives is open and is Ben's: a section on the building Selection card (per-building, where the number's grain actually is), a view on the Corporation dashboard beside the existing Workforce roll-up card, or a surface of its own. What is settled is only that it has no home today and that the Budget ledger's Wages tier currently has no visible consequence anywhere.

items.title: The Construction ledger gets two tabs, and one construction element with two doors
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, designing slot 3 after moving Construction there: "This ledger should hold two tabs. First a list of all building types where the player owns one building (Buildings). And a second tab for construction, our presently pre-existing empty queue (Construction)."

AND THE RECONCILIATION, which is the load-bearing half: "We want to reconcile our tile-selection construction ledger with the queue. For this, we can make sure the construction queue is collapsible, and place it above the existing tile-selection construction ledger, wiring both clicks to the same element. (slot 3, and construction button on that tile)."

SO: ONE construction element, TWO doors. The Construction tab draws a COLLAPSIBLE queue, then `draw_construction_ledger` (selection_panel.cpp:3658 — the tile-selection build front door, whose function name is already the phrase Ben used). The nav-rail slot-3 press and the tile Selection card's construction button both open that same tab. No second code path, no duplicated build bar.

THE GENERALISATION PROBLEM IS BEN'S OWN, RAISED WITH THE DESIGN: the construction element now has to render with a tile selected and with none. His recommendation, and it is ACCEPTED here: an explicit "Select a tile" response where the build bar would be.

IT IS ACCEPTED FOR A PRINCIPLED REASON RATHER THAN FOR WANT OF A BETTER IDEA, and the reason is the ruling Ben gave in the same message. A richer empty state would have to list tiles the player COULD build on — and any ordering of that list is a recommendation, which is precisely what he rejected the build-opportunity surface for ("it enters the territory of telling the player what to do"). There is no way to fill this empty state that is not the thing we just declined. "Select a tile" is therefore correct, not a placeholder. Contrast BL-682 (buildings by type), where the equivalent empty state CAN be improved, because navigating buildings the player already owns is not a recommendation. The two empty states differ for that reason and should not be made uniform.

WHY THE QUEUE IS COLLAPSIBLE: it is empty most of the time (NR-718 — BL-176 diagnosed exactly this and its fix was deleted with the Buildings tab in the 2026-08-15 rework). Collapsed, an empty queue costs one line instead of owning the surface; the build bar below it is then what a player meets.

CLEAR THE DEAD STATE WHILE HERE (NR-718): `construction.panel_view` is write-only — verify_api.cpp:2241 sets it, nothing in src/ reads it — and it carries a long comment describing the two-view panel that was removed. `construction.panel_focus_building` is referenced nowhere. The two tabs give `panel_view` a real subject again, so it is revived rather than deleted; its comment must be rewritten to describe THESE two views, and `panel_focus_building` deleted unless BL-682 gives it one.

The tab strip follows the standing toggle rule: re-clicking the ACTIVE tab closes the ledger, switching between tabs is an ordinary view change. Default tab is Buildings, for NR-718's reason — the player always owns buildings and usually has nothing building.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Two tabs on a revived `construction.panel_view` (0 Construction / 1 Buildings, default Buildings), its dead comment rewritten; `panel_focus_building` deleted, the drill keying off `selected_entity` instead. The Construction tab draws a collapsed-by-default queue then the build bar. `ui_state::show_build_ledger` is GONE — the build bar became an inline section rather than a second column tenant, which is what made ONE element with two doors possible rather than two implementations. Assertion C9 presses the tile card's Construct button from an empty column and reads back `open_panel == "construction"`, `view == 0`: the two-doors claim, which no capture can make.

items.title: The Buildings tab - the player's estate grouped by type, with count and total profit
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "the general form building screen can group all selected (if no selection then all) buildings by type, and then display roughly 9 buildings with a vertical scroll. Each should have a count and total profit. When expanded, we should see 'Select a tile'. If a tile is selected, we should see production methods, workforce, and any other building levers."

THE ROSTER: one row per building TYPE the player owns at least one of. Each row carries a COUNT and a TOTAL PROFIT (the type's buildings summed — `rank_player_buildings_by_profit` / `building_profit.hpp` already compute the per-building figure the Balance ledger ranks on). About nine rows visible with a vertical scroll. Grouped over the SELECTED buildings where there is a selection, over all of them where there is not.

EXPANDING A ROW shows the per-building levers — production method, workforce, and the rest of what the building Selection card carries. Those levers need ONE building, so with no tile selected there is nothing to draw them for.

PROPOSED IMPROVEMENT ON THE EMPTY STATE, and it needs Ben's nod. Rather than "Select a tile", have an expanded type row LIST ITS OWN BUILDINGS — one line each, tile and individual profit, summing visibly to the total on the group header — and let a press select one, which then draws the levers. The chain becomes type -> building -> levers without leaving the ledger.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE THING BEN JUST REJECTED. It ranks nothing and recommends nothing: it lists what the player already owns so they can reach one of them. That is navigation. The build-opportunity surface was declined because ordering tiles by expected return decides the question the player is there to answer; a list of your own four extraction sites decides nothing. The distinction is now written into CONCEPT.md § Player identity.

It also removes a dead end. "Select a tile" is an instruction with no affordance attached — the player must leave the ledger, find the building on the map, and come back. Since the group header already asserts a count, the buildings behind it are exactly the set the ledger has in hand.

FALL BACK TO BEN'S ORIGINAL if he prefers: an expanded row with no selection reads "Select a tile" and nothing else. That is one function either way.

RETIRED, NOT DEFERRED. This item originally carried Ben's "For the buildings tab in this ledger, we will want to wire a button into the tile selection element, however we can leave that for now." That button was then split in two by what followed, and the two halves ended differently:
  - The BUILDING card's grid button is BUILT — BL-684 (grid door to levers), un-deferred the same day once BL-683 took the levers off that card and made the gap real.
  - The TILE card's button is RETIRED. Ben, 2026-08-29: "Don't wire the tile cards, just building is fine." Not deferred, not pending — do not build it, and do not read the sentence above as outstanding work.

THE LEVERS MOVE HERE RATHER THAN BEING SHARED FROM THE SELECTION CARD. My first draft of this item said to call into the card's accordion pages; Ben overruled it the same day: "I prefer if our selection card's centre element always holds/presents data, and never levers. So therefore I'd recommend moving levers to our buildings ledger." BL-683 (levers leave selection) owns that move and this tab is its destination. Still ONE implementation - the same `draw_production_method_section` and `draw_building_workforce_page` bodies, relocated, never a second set of controls writing the same fields.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Roster grouped by display name with count and sign-coloured total; expansion lists members with their own nets and a press selects one. Deterministic ordering by name, then net, then id. THE AGENT DECLINED HALF OF ONE SENTENCE OF THE SPEC AND WAS RIGHT TO. Ben wrote "group all selected (if no selection then all) buildings by type", but selection is single-entity, so grouping over it collapses the roster to one row UNDER THE VERY PRESS THAT SELECTED THE BUILDING — destroying the navigation this item exists for. Built as: always the whole estate, with selection driving which group expands and which row highlights. Raised as an open question in construction.md rather than silently substituted. Type rows sort ALPHABETICALLY, not by profit — a conservative reading of the CONCEPT.md ranking line, also raised rather than assumed.

items.title: The Selection card's centre presents data only - Method and Workforce move to the Buildings ledger
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "I prefer if our selection card's centre element always holds/presents data, and never levers. So therefore I'd recommend moving levers to our buildings ledger."

IT REVERSES A DATED RULING OF HIS OWN, and that is recorded rather than quietly applied. SELECTION.md carried "There is no Manage link - every control it would route to lives on this card (Ben, NR-245)", and the 2026-08-15 rework moved Method, Workforce and Lifecycle ONTO the card on that basis. Newest-dated wins. What NR-245 was actually avoiding still holds: there is no Manage link and no round trip through a second surface, because the ledger that now holds the levers is reachable from the card's own action grid.

WHAT MOVES - the two centre pages whose whole content is a control:
  - Method (`building_page_kind::method`, `draw_production_method_section`) - the tiled recipe grid with its Switch buttons, calling `try_switch_recipe`.
  - Workforce (`building_page_kind::workforce`, `draw_building_workforce_page`) - the 0-100 slider writing `workforce_target` and clearing `workforce_auto`.

WHAT STAYS - the pages that report:
  - Profitability (charts: revenue vs segmented expenses, the net line, the input basket).
  - Status (construction rate/ETA, or "Operating."). It is also the ONLY page a rival building gets, and that short-circuit must survive the move untouched.

THE BOUNDARY RUNS AROUND THE CENTRE, NOT AROUND THE ELEMENT. The right-hand 2x3 ACTION GRID keeps its buttons - Mothball, Dismantle and the workforce Auto toggle are in the designated action area, not the centre, so Ben's rule does not touch them. Do not "finish the job" by moving the grid; that would leave the card with no way to act at all and is not what was ruled.

ONE IMPLEMENTATION, NOT TWO. The moved pages must be RELOCATED, not reimplemented: the same `draw_production_method_section` and `draw_building_workforce_page` bodies, called from the ledger. Two sets of controls writing `workforce_target` and `try_switch_recipe` is how two surfaces come to disagree, and this project has already paid for that shape once.

THE FULL-CANVAS TAKEOVER FOLLOWS THE PAGES. `draw_building_page_expanded` (selection_card.cpp) reads the same `building_pages()` / `draw_building_page()` list+dispatch pair as the in-band accordion, so removing two entries changes both surfaces at once - which is correct, and worth knowing before the diff looks larger than expected.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH RAISING WITH BEN RATHER THAN SOLVING SILENTLY: with the levers gone, a building the player selects on the MAP no longer offers any way to act on it from the card. The route becomes select-then-open-the-ledger. Whether the action grid should therefore carry a fourth button that opens the Buildings ledger aimed at this building is the obvious follow-on - and is exactly the button Ben deferred in BL-682 ("we will want to wire a button into the tile selection element, however we can leave that for now"). Deferred, not forgotten.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. `building_page_kind` is now {profitability, status}; `draw_production_method_section` and `draw_building_workforce_page` are called from the ledger — same bodies, relocated not reimplemented. The rival short-circuit survives untouched and now carries a comment saying why it is a guarantee rather than a convenience. The 2x3 action grid is otherwise unchanged, the boundary running around the centre and not the element. ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: Status is now reachable on a player card. Before, Workforce always applied so the page list was never empty and Status was dead for a player building; it is now the honest fallback when there is no profit estimate.

items.title: A fourth action-grid button opens the Buildings tab aimed at this building
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DEFERRED, THEN UN-DEFERRED THE SAME DAY. Ben, 2026-08-29, filing BL-682: "we will want to wire a button into the tile selection element, however we can leave that for now." Then, after the levers-move ruling made the gap concrete: "And wire in the fourth grid button, you're right that now is a fine time to do so."

WHAT CHANGED IN BETWEEN, and it is the whole justification: BL-683 (levers leave selection) takes Method and Workforce off the building Selection card. Deferring this button cost nothing while the levers were still on the card. The moment they leave, a building selected on the MAP has no route to its own levers at all — select it, notice they are gone, open the ledger, find it again. The batch that creates the gap should close it.

A fourth button in the building Selection card's right-hand 2x3 action grid, opening the Buildings tab of the slot-3 ledger AIMED at the building whose card it sits on. Three of the six cells are used (Mothball, Dismantle, Auto), so there is room without a layout change.

AIMED, NOT MERELY OPENED. Landing the player on a roster of every type, having pressed a button on a specific building, would leave them finding what they already had selected. It opens with that building's TYPE GROUP expanded and the building selected, so its levers are on screen in one press. `selected_entity` is already the card's subject, so this is routing plus expanding the right group.

IT IS A DOOR, NOT A TOGGLE. The standing toggle rule binds controls whose active state is visible; this one has none. It opens the ledger and does not close it on a second press.

ITS OWN GLYPH. Two lit controls must not share a silhouette (BL-174, nav-rail legibility), and this sits inches from Mothball and Dismantle.

ABSENT ON A RIVAL BUILDING. The Buildings tab is the player's own estate. The rival card already short-circuits to a single Status page under the competitor-visibility rule; the grid must keep the same discipline rather than offering a door to a surface that would have nothing to show. That absence is the assertion most worth writing, because the alternative is a player discovering it.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24, in the same batch that created the gap it closes. `glyph_roster` — a panel outline with one row picked out, sharing no silhouette. Aimed: expands the type group, keeps the building selected, levers on screen in one press. A door, not a toggle. ABSENT on a rival card, falling back to `glyph_reserved` with no reflow — asserted (C6) rather than left for a player to discover.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The clearing tick retains a per-exchange record
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, choosing it over shipping Trades without history: add a per-exchange record to the clearing loop in this batch.

THE SHAPE IS DEFINED IN `MARKETS.md` § The exchange record and both agents build to it: tick, market, resource, quantity, unit_price, seller, buyer. Ring-capped the way the plot histories are.

IT RECORDS REVENUE, NOT PROFIT, AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL. `stockpile_component` is `quantities[]` and nothing else — there is NO cost basis anywhere in the model. A unit of ore in a pool does not know what it cost to extract or buy, so the margin on selling it cannot be derived from the sale. `quantity * unit_price` is honest; profit is not available at this grain and MUST NOT be printed as though it were. The two routes to a real margin (a weighted-average cost basis on the pool, or answering margin at the building where `building_profit.hpp` already nets it) are both larger than this record and neither is in scope.

`unit_price` is the price CLEARING RESOLVED, not the floor the order carried. An order is honoured at clearing, so what a seller asked and what they got are different numbers and only one of them is the trade.

SERIALISATION IS THE RISK. The record is world state, so it enters the save envelope and `save_game_version` moves. NR-708 records that NO envelope field has round-trip coverage and that `read_save_game` refuses the whole file on a version mismatch — every existing save becomes unreadable, which follows the file's own conventions but is worth knowing rather than discovering. THIS IS THE CHANGE THAT SHOULD BRING AN ENVELOPE ROUND-TRIP ASSERTION WITH IT, on the font_glyph_harness precedent, rather than adding one more untested field to a seam that has never been tested.

Determinism: the append order must be a total order over the clearing walk, not whatever the market map iterates in. A record whose row order varies by platform is a record that cannot be asserted against.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Merged and verified in the main session. exchange_record carries tick, market, resource, quantity, unit_price, seller, buyer - the shape MARKETS.md defined, unchanged - held as world::exchanges, an 8192-row ring with oldest_first() because the raw vector stops being chronological once it wraps. ONE SHAPE DECISION THE DOC DID NOT SETTLE AND THE AGENT TOOK CORRECTLY: only the matched order-book path has a real corp on both sides, and that path is dormant in play; the three paths carrying the volume trade against the market, so seller or buyer is null_entity meaning THE MARKET, not unknown. Recording only matched trades would have left the Trades tab permanently empty. Written into MARKETS.md. Determinism: append order is a total order over the clearing walk, asserted against a reversed unordered_map insertion - the half that fails a hash-order walk. The record is deliberately NOT folded into state_hash, being a consequence of state the hash already covers. world_save_version 18 -> 19 rather than save_game_version, since world state belongs in the world snapshot. THE ENVELOPE ROUND-TRIP NOW EXISTS (save_envelope_roundtrip, 20 rows PASS) - NR-708 had recorded that no envelope field had ever had coverage, and this is the change that brought it. Verified here: BUILD_OK, exchange_record_harness PASS, save_envelope_roundtrip PASS. Two red harnesses confirmed NOT caused by this: spectator_determinism (stale golden, already NR-661) and quarterly_return R2 (unowned, now NR-720) - the latter checked by reading the diff rather than re-running the agent experiment: the whole change is one lambda that appends, with no arithmetic, so a budget identity cannot be broken by it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The Goods table - one row per good, graph flattened into the row
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "we will flatten graphs for each good. They can fit into the same row as the header... With item_glyph; name; price; body_average_price; price_relative_to_base_price; six_month_price_graph."

THE GRAPH WINDOW IS **8 QUARTERS**, not six months — Ben's answer once the arithmetic was put to him. `record_histories` samples ONCE PER ECON TICK and a tick is a calendar quarter, so six months is two data points. The ring caps at 64, so 8 of 64 is a recent-window read.

COLUMNS: item glyph, name, price, body average price, price vs base, 8-quarter graph. `price vs base` is `price[r] / base_price[r]`, already to hand. `body_average_price` is the one new derivation — mean `price[r]` across the markets on the selected body — and is the first column to drop IF the row will not fit. Measure before dropping it: at 384 px the pressure is on the graph's width, not the column count, so dropping a text column buys the graph very little. Show both if it is close.

THE ITEM GLYPH IS A PLACEHOLDER (Ben, 2026-08-29 — flags and glyphs are a later sprint). The settled design is four value-track silhouettes, `ICONS.md` § 2b. Two conditions: the placeholder must LOOK provisional rather than be learned as meaningful, and the column must reserve the REAL glyph's width so the table is not laid out twice.

ROW HEIGHT IS THE OPEN MEASUREMENT. Ben: "let's compare this at 8 rows, 10 rows, and 12 rows." Build all three and capture at **1920x1080** — a density judgement at 720p is taken against half the content height, which is how every such number this sprint was got wrong before 2026-08-29.

WHAT THIS REPLACES AND WHY IT IS NOT ONLY DENSITY: the stacked sparklines gave every good its own implicit scale, so goods could not be compared — the one thing a price board is for — and gave no direction at all. Fix the scale and the direction, not just the row count.

AND NOTHING HAS EVER SEEN PAST GOOD 4 (NR-719). The scroll hook aimed at the outer window while the sparklines sat in an inner child scroller, so the "foot" capture was byte-identical to the head. Whatever is wrong below the fold is unexamined; fix `scroll_panel` to reach the real scroller (and to REJECT an unknown name loudly rather than silently clearing the request) as part of this.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. The Goods table: one row per traded good — glyph, name, price, vs base, 8-quarter graph flattened into the row. Verified here: goods_table 8/8, 45 rows for 45 traded goods, every price and base matching `market_component`, `vs base` exact to 0.000000, every row plotting exactly 8 samples. `scroll_panel` fixed to reach the inner scroller and to FAIL LOUDLY on an unknown name, which immediately exposed a third instance of NR-719: `scroll_panel("construction")` mapped to a window named "Building" that has NEVER existed. BODY_AVERAGE_PRICE DID NOT SURVIVE, and my prediction was wrong — I said the pressure would be on the graph width, not the column count. Measured at 1920x1080 over the real 45-good roster: with the column the name field is 42 px and 13 of 45 names fit; without it 98 px and 36 of 45. The graph is only ~3.4 em. Off by default behind a flag; the script prints both layouts every run.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The Trades tab - my positions, the market's positions, and what I could be doing
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, reworking Sell Orders: "we should rework this into persistent trades... What we really want to see is a list of trades, and their profits. We also want to see potential trades and their profits."

THREE READS, KEPT VISIBLY DISTINCT (`MARKETS.md` § Trades). They are not equally cheap and the surface must not present them as one table:
  1. MY STANDING TRADES — every order the player's corp holds here. Exists today; this is the old Sell Orders view with the buy side admitted.
  2. THE MARKET'S STANDING TRADES — every order here, whoever owns it. **THE GATE IS: the player owns a building on that body** (Ben, 2026-08-29, choosing it over "an order here", "either", and "any discovered market"). Orders are world state and are the deliberate public signal, so this is a reading question, not a disclosure one — but the gate is real and must be enforced, not assumed.
  3. POTENTIAL TRADES — a derivation, not a record: buy price here against sell price there, less the haulage the route would cost.

THE HISTORY HALF READS BL-685's EXCHANGE RECORD, and the column is **revenue**, never profit. There is no cost basis in the model — `stockpile_component` is `quantities[]` — so margin is not derivable from a sale. Printing a "profit" the clearing loop never computed would be inventing a number a player would act on, which the honest-placeholder idiom does not licence.

RANKING IS PERMITTED HERE and this is the one surface where that has been ruled on explicitly. `CONCEPT.md` § Player identity: rank where the top row is one input among several, not where it IS the move. Ben: "Market prices is a vital pillar of gameplay, but the strategy 'just build the most profitable' is a red herring." So potential trades may be sorted by margin.

Ben on the tab as a whole: "Since this doesn't exist, just give a go, and I can refine later." Build the derivable halves properly, wire history to the new record, and show him before going further.

THE TAB IS CALLED **TRADES** (Ben, 2026-08-29, explicitly: "Rename for BL-687, we should call it Trades"). Not Sell Orders, and not Orders. The word carries the widening: a sell order is one direction and one actor, a trade is a position either way round held by anyone in the market. The rail, the tab strip, `question_log.json`, `ACTIONS.json` and `market.md` all say Trades.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The nation presence row - who operates in this market
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "a list of nations who operate in that market. This can be a wrapped row of flags for each nation, wrapping to 2 or 3 rows if needed... And this should sit between body/market selection and our tabs."

POSITION IS PART OF THE SPEC: below the Body and Market combos, above the Goods / Trades tab strip.

THERE ARE NO FLAGS. `nation_colour(entity_id)` is a palette colour and is all that exists — corps carry an emblem tag, nations do not. The row is COLOURED CHIPS with the nation's initials, named on hover (`ICONS.md` § 2b). Real per-nation emblem artwork would be a generated identity system, a feature of its own; do not stub one glyph and call it a flag. Ben, same day: flags and glyphs are a later sprint, use placeholders.

Wrap to two or three rows if it must, though the doc notes that is unlikely at the current nation count.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Coloured chips with initials between the Body/Market combos and the tab strip — six on the home market. NO STORE ANSWERS "which nations operate here", so it is derived: building tile -> `market_for_tile` -> `tile_to_nation`. A real bug surfaced doing it, worth keeping: `w.buildings` is keyed by BUILDING id, not tile id, and the first cut read the key as a tile — which silently produced "No national presence." on every market rather than failing. Flags remain placeholders per Ben; the settled design is four value-track silhouettes in a later sprint.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Convoys becomes its own ledger at rail slot 7
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "I think we can make convoys into a ledger of its own", then "give convoys a slot, put it after market", then — asked whether it lands in this batch — yes, same batch.

IT MUST BE THIS BATCH, and that is the reason rather than a preference: the Market flattening DELETES the third tab. Without a home, Convoys is either a regression or a tab the design says should not exist. The docs for it are already written (`convoys.md`).

RAIL SLOT 7, directly after Market, taking the rail to FOURTEEN. Everything from Corp. Strategy down shifts one: Corp. Strategy 8, Diplomacy 9, History 10, developer tail 11-13, Contracts 14. `tab_count` 13 -> 14. MENU.md is already updated to describe this; the code has to catch up.

It draws `icons::convoy` — the marker the canvas already uses for cargo in transit, so slot and canvas share a silhouette. No new glyph. Arms `supply_routes` on open, which is the pairing a tab strip could never give it: opening the Market ledger armed the price wash instead.

ONE FLAT VIEW. No Body/Market selectors — a convoy is a route between two places and is not scoped by the market you are looking at, which is part of why the tab sat oddly there.

TWO INHERITED DEFECTS, both in `convoys.md`. Destinations clip (NR-709's family, four surfaces now). And a row reads `Agricultural Produce x0` — a zero-quantity convoy in flight with a haul cost paid and a progress bar running. MEASURE THAT BEFORE REBUILDING AROUND IT: it is not a display bug, the display is reporting what it was given. If dispatch can legitimately commit an empty convoy the row must say why; if it cannot, this is a supply-layer bug the ledger merely revealed. Report the finding either way.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Convoys at rail slot 7, the rail to fourteen. Verified here: convoys_ledger 23/23 — slot 7 opens it, arms `supply_routes` from a non-supply-routes starting lens, re-press closes it, and ALL FOURTEEN SLOTS ARE VERIFIED BY PRESS rather than by name, which is what NR-716 said shell_pass could not do. THE x0 CONVOY IS A ROUNDING DEFECT, NOT A SUPPLY BUG, and the premise I wrote into convoys.md was wrong: I said the display was reporting what it was given; it was ROUNDING what it was given. Measured over 5 seeds x 20 ticks (`convoy_cargo_census`, new): 1669 convoys dispatched, ZERO with an empty hold, 77 (4.6%) carrying a positive cargo below 0.5 that `"x%.0f"` renders as x0 — min 0.0097, median 5.62. Neither dispatch path can commit an empty convoy. The row now tiers precision against that distribution and the harness asserts the no-empty-hold invariant permanently. ALSO CAUGHT AND FIXED IN-BATCH: the 14th slot put its centre at y=746 against the 720 px floor, leaving Contracts drawn and unreachable — invisible at 1080p, so only the resolution PAIR could catch it (NR-723).

FOUR SITES, THREE SURFACES, verified by grep rather than remembered:
  - `balance_ledger.cpp:258` — "Policy levers - not yet wired (BL-155)"
  - `balance_ledger.cpp:146` — the same id inside a tooltip
  - `tech_tree_panel.cpp:599` — "BL-087 design mock - read-only."
  - `tile_inspector.cpp:245` — "First cut (BL-660)…" on the Tectonics view

THE LAST ONE LANDED THE DAY BEFORE THIS SWEEP, which is the argument for doing it now: this is a pattern still being copied, not a legacy to tidy. A backlog id is internal bookkeeping and means nothing to a player; what the line is actually trying to say — that a control is not yet wired, or a surface is a mock — is worth saying in words.

Keep the honesty, drop the reference. "Not yet wired to the economy" says everything "(BL-155)" was doing and says it to someone who can read it.

items.title: The Corporation ledger answers "how well am I doing?" and keeps one card
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "each of our ledgers answers certain questions, and I'm struggling to think of interesting questions on the Corporation ledger. It should be a space for 'How well am I doing?', since the data currently shown is essentially better off elsewhere. For now, keep only Finance, but rename it to 'Balance'. We can condense it to a column chart showing earnings and stacked expenses. So just two bars."

THE QUESTION IS THE POINT, and it is why three of four cards go. Production, Trade and Workforce are each answered better elsewhere — Production and Workforce by the Construction ledger's Buildings tab (which now holds the estate AND the levers), Trade by the Market and Convoys ledgers. What is left that only this surface can answer is "how well am I doing?", and the honest answer to that today is money.

ONE CARD: Finance, renamed **Balance**, condensed to a two-bar column chart — earnings as one bar, expenses stacked as segments beside it.

THE CHART ALREADY EXISTS AT A DIFFERENT GRAIN AND MUST NOT BE REIMPLEMENTED. `draw_revenue_expense_bars` (selection_panel.cpp:190) draws exactly this for a BUILDING — revenue as one plain bar, `input_cost` / `maintenance` / `wages` stacked as three shaded segments, with a hovered segment naming itself. The corp version is the same drawing over `corp_budget` instead of `building_profit`. GENERALISE the drawer to take the numbers rather than a `building_profit`, and call it from both. Two implementations of one chart is how two surfaces come to disagree, and this project has already paid for that shape twice this sprint.

The corp's expense set is wider than a building's: income against inputs bought, maintenance, wages, and interest. Interest is hidden at zero (`balance.md` § Data sources records that the row count changes across the solvency boundary) — so the stack has a variable segment count, which the building version does not. That is the one real difference and it belongs in the shared drawer, not in a fork.

DEFERRED, EXPLICITLY AND BY BEN: research points, score/ranking, market cap and other heuristics. His words — "essentially, we will revisit this once core gameplay is established." DO NOT BUILD THEM. They are recorded here so the intent survives, not so the next session starts them; several have no store behind them at all (there is no score, no ranking and no market cap in the model, and RP is a stub — `RESEARCH.md`).

A NAMING COLLISION RAISED, AND SETTLED BY BEN THE SAME DAY. I raised that "Balance Ledger" is already slot 2's source name — the rail calls slot 2 "Budget", and `MENU.md` § Menu set records that widening deliberately ("Budget (not Balance Ledger)") — so a "Balance" card in slot 1 puts the word on two money surfaces in adjacent slots. The internal risk was the larger one: a reader meeting `balance_ledger.cpp` (slot 2) and a "Balance" card (slot 1) is in the NR-704 situation, where two things named alike drove a defect past two independent guards.

BEN'S RULING, 2026-08-29: *"This is called the 'Corporation' ledger, it just has that 'Balance' sub-header. If the data is in both places, that's fine. We can revisit the 'Budget' ledger later."* The LEDGER is Corporation; Balance is a sub-header inside it, not a competing surface name. Settled — do not re-raise it, and do not rename it in a later tidy.

THE OVERLAP WITH THE BUDGET LEDGER IS THEREFORE ACCEPTED, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS AN EXCEPTION WORTH NAMING. This same sprint deleted the entire Economy panel for duplicating Balance and Corporation, and the ledger docs carry a hard "no two surfaces answer the same question" line. Ben is relaxing it here on purpose, with Budget to be revisited later. It is an accepted overlap with a date on it — not an oversight to clean up, and not a general licence to duplicate elsewhere.

The resting/expanded gap is what the whole item is about. Measured at 1920x1080: four verdict lines and roughly 700 px of empty column beneath them, in the first slot on the rail — the one density complaint this sprint that got WORSE at Ben's resolution rather than dissolving. The expanded drill is the best-reading surface in the app; the resting state was the odd one out.

Fix `Workforce 82% of labour demand m` on the way past if the card survives in any form — it clips mid-word at both resolutions. If Workforce goes entirely, the clip goes with it.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Merged and verified in the main session: BUILD_OK, corp_dashboard 10/10, construction_ledger_tabs 41/41, and every surface sharing the drawer green. One card, Balance, drawing a two-bar column chart that fills the column — the ~700 px void is gone. THE CHART BECAME A SHARED DRAWER RATHER THAN A FORK: `ui::charts::draw_stacked_columns` over a new `stack_segment`, with the building card's `draw_revenue_expense_bars` reduced to an adapter. The variable segment count lives in the drawer — a stack of several skips its zeros, a LONE column is exempt because a lone column is a plain bar and draws its own zero, which is what keeps the building card byte-identical. Two measured refinements past the first draft: auto-fit columns (97 px against the building's 44 px cap) and a `tight_axis` opt-in, because `nice_ceil(58.7)` is 100 and left 41% of the plot empty on the surface built to fix empty space. Interest absent solvent, present at 74.64 in debt with the stack growing by exactly one segment. The Workforce clip is gone WITH the card — confirmed by absence of the string, not assumed. NR-724 filed: deleting the Production card orphaned BL-591's growth-track readout, and two live docs still assert it exists; the agent correctly refused to resolve that. THE LIVE CLICK IS OWED.
